title: IL HB1806: THERAPY RESOURCES OVERSIGHT

obligations: A licensed professional using artificial intelligence to assist in providing supplementary support where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed must inform the patient or the patient's legally authorized representative in writing that artificial intelligence will be used and the specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool or system, and must obtain consent to the use of artificial intelligence (Sec. 15(b)).

A licensed professional using artificial intelligence must maintain full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use associated with the system and satisfy the requirements of subsection (b) (Sec. 15(a)).
A licensed professional may use artificial intelligence only to the extent the use meets the requirements of Section 15 (Sec. 20(b)).

All records kept by a licensed professional and all communications between an individual seeking therapy or psychotherapy services and a licensed professional shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed except as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Sec. 25).
Any individual, corporation, or entity found in violation of this Act shall pay the civil penalty within 60 days after the date of an order by the Department imposing the civil penalty (Sec. 30(a)).
Therapy or psychotherapy services must be conducted by an individual who is a licensed professional (Sec. 20(a)).
prohibitions: An individual, corporation, or entity may not provide, advertise, or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet based artificial intelligence, to the public in this State unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are conducted by an individual who is a licensed professional (Sec. 20(a)).
A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to make independent therapeutic decisions (Sec. 20(b)(1)).
A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to directly interact with clients in any form of therapeutic communication (Sec. 20(b)(2)).
A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without review and approval by the licensed professional (Sec. 20(b)(3)).
A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to detect emotions or mental states (Sec. 20(b)(4)).
All records and communications shall not be disclosed except as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Sec. 25).

No licensed professional shall be permitted to use artificial intelligence to assist in providing supplementary support where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed unless the patient or the patient's legally authorized representative is informed in writing and provides consent (Sec. 15(b)).

What it does

This Act safeguards individuals seeking therapy or psychotherapy services by requiring those services to be delivered by licensed or certified professionals. It protects consumers from unlicensed or unqualified providers, including unregulated artificial intelligence systems, while respecting individual choice and access to community based and faith based mental health support. It permits licensed professionals to use artificial intelligence only for administrative or supplementary support, with written notice and consent for recording or transcription, and prohibits artificial intelligence from engaging in therapeutic communication or independent decisions.

Who it applies to

  • Individuals, corporations, and entities that provide, advertise, or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services in Illinois
  • Licensed professionals using artificial intelligence in therapy or psychotherapy services
  • The Department of Financial and Professional Regulation for enforcement and penalties

Effective date

upon becoming law

Key definitions

  • Administrative support: tasks performed to assist a licensed professional in the delivery of therapy or psychotherapy services that do not involve communication, including managing appointment scheduling and reminders, processing billing and insurance claims, and drafting general communications related to therapy logistics that do not include therapeutic advice (Sec. 10)
  • Artificial intelligence: has the meaning given to that term in Section 2-101 of the Illinois Human Rights Act (Sec. 10)
  • Consent: a clear, explicit affirmative act by an individual that unambiguously communicates the individual's express, freely given, informed, voluntary, specific, and unambiguous written agreement, including a written agreement provided by electronic means, and is revocable by the individual; does not include acceptance of general or broad terms of use, hovering over, muting, pausing, or closing digital content, or agreement obtained through deceptive actions (Sec. 10)
  • Department: the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (Sec. 10)
  • Licensed professional: an individual who holds a valid license issued by this State to provide therapy or psychotherapy services, including licensed clinical psychologist, licensed clinical social worker, licensed social worker, licensed professional counselor, licensed clinical professional counselor, licensed marriage and family therapist, certified alcohol and other drug counselor authorized to provide therapy or psychotherapy services, licensed professional music therapist, licensed advanced practice psychiatric nurse as defined in Section 1-101.3 of the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code, and any other professional authorized by this State to provide therapy or psychotherapy services, except for a physician (Sec. 10)
  • Peer support: services provided by individuals with lived experience of mental health conditions or recovery from substance use that are intended to offer encouragement, understanding, and guidance without clinical intervention (Sec. 10)
  • Religious counseling: counseling provided by clergy members, pastoral counselors, or other religious leaders acting within the scope of their religious duties if the services are explicitly faith based and are not represented as clinical mental health services or therapy or psychotherapy services (Sec. 10)
  • Supplementary support: tasks performed to assist a licensed professional in the delivery of therapy or psychotherapy services that do not involve therapeutic communication and that are not administrative support, including preparing and maintaining client records, including therapy notes; analyzing anonymized data to track client progress or identify trends, subject to review by a licensed professional; and identifying and organizing external resources or referrals for client use (Sec. 10)
  • Therapeutic communication: any verbal, non verbal, or written interaction conducted in a clinical or professional setting that is intended to diagnose, treat, or address an individual's mental, emotional, or behavioral health concerns, including direct interactions with clients for the purpose of understanding or reflecting their thoughts, emotions, or experiences; providing guidance, therapeutic strategies, or interventions designed to achieve mental health outcomes; offering emotional support, reassurance, or empathy in response to psychological or emotional distress; collaborating with clients to develop or modify therapeutic goals or treatment plans; and offering behavioral feedback intended to promote psychological growth or address mental health conditions (Sec. 10)
  • Therapy or psychotherapy services: services provided to diagnose, treat, or improve an individual's mental health or behavioral health; does not include religious counseling or peer support (Sec. 10)

Obligations

  • A licensed professional using artificial intelligence to assist in providing supplementary support where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed must inform the patient or the patient's legally authorized representative in writing that artificial intelligence will be used and the specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool or system, and must obtain consent to the use of artificial intelligence (Sec. 15(b)).
  • A licensed professional using artificial intelligence must maintain full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use associated with the system and satisfy the requirements of subsection (b) (Sec. 15(a)).
  • A licensed professional may use artificial intelligence only to the extent the use meets the requirements of Section 15 (Sec. 20(b)).
  • All records kept by a licensed professional and all communications between an individual seeking therapy or psychotherapy services and a licensed professional shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed except as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Sec. 25).
  • Any individual, corporation, or entity found in violation of this Act shall pay the civil penalty within 60 days after the date of an order by the Department imposing the civil penalty (Sec. 30(a)).
  • Therapy or psychotherapy services must be conducted by an individual who is a licensed professional (Sec. 20(a)).

Prohibitions

  • An individual, corporation, or entity may not provide, advertise, or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet based artificial intelligence, to the public in this State unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are conducted by an individual who is a licensed professional (Sec. 20(a)).
  • A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to make independent therapeutic decisions (Sec. 20(b)(1)).
  • A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to directly interact with clients in any form of therapeutic communication (Sec. 20(b)(2)).
  • A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without review and approval by the licensed professional (Sec. 20(b)(3)).
  • A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to detect emotions or mental states (Sec. 20(b)(4)).
  • All records and communications shall not be disclosed except as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Sec. 25).
  • No licensed professional shall be permitted to use artificial intelligence to assist in providing supplementary support where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed unless the patient or the patient's legally authorized representative is informed in writing and provides consent (Sec. 15(b)).

Penalties and enforcement

The Department of Financial and Professional Regulation enforces this Act and has authority to investigate any actual, alleged, or suspected violation (Sec. 30(b)). Any individual, corporation, or entity found in violation shall pay a civil penalty to the Department in an amount not to exceed $10,000 per violation, as determined by the Department, with penalties assessed based on the degree of harm and the circumstances of the violation; the civil penalty is assessed after a hearing in accordance with Section 2105-100 of the Department of Professional Regulation Law of the Civil Administrative Code of Illinois, and the order constitutes a judgment and may be filed and executed in the same manner as any judgment from a court of record (Sec. 30(a)). Private right of action: not stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying artificial intelligence to provide, advertise, or offer therapy or psychotherapy services in Illinois must ensure those services are conducted by a licensed professional; otherwise the deployment is prohibited (Sec. 20(a)).
  • Artificial intelligence may be used only for administrative support or supplementary support by a licensed professional, and the licensed professional must maintain full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use (Sec. 15(a)).
  • If artificial intelligence is used to assist supplementary support where a session is recorded or transcribed, the organisation must provide written notice of the artificial intelligence use and its specific purpose and obtain consent from the patient or representative (Sec. 15(b)).
  • Artificial intelligence cannot directly interact with clients in therapeutic communication, make independent therapeutic decisions, generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without licensed professional review and approval, or detect emotions or mental states (Sec. 20(b)).
  • Records and communications must remain confidential and may be disclosed only as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Sec. 25).
  • Violations can result in civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation, assessed by the Department after a hearing (Sec. 30(a)).

Notable exemptions

  • Religious counseling (Sec. 35(1)).
  • Peer support (Sec. 35(2)).
  • Self help materials and educational resources that are available to the public and do not purport to offer therapy or psychotherapy services (Sec. 35(3)).
  • Therapy or psychotherapy services does not include religious counseling or peer support (Sec. 10).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the organisation provides, advertises, or offers therapy or psychotherapy services in Illinois; if so, ensure all such services are conducted by licensed professionals (Sec. 20(a)).
  • If using artificial intelligence, limit its use to administrative support or supplementary support by a licensed professional, and ensure the licensed professional maintains full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use (Sec. 15(a)).
  • If artificial intelligence is used for supplementary support where a session is recorded or transcribed, provide written notice to the patient or legally authorized representative of the artificial intelligence use and its specific purpose, and obtain consent (Sec. 15(b)).
  • Prohibit artificial intelligence from making independent therapeutic decisions, directly interacting with clients in therapeutic communication, generating therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without licensed professional review and approval, or detecting emotions or mental states (Sec. 20(b)).
  • Maintain confidentiality of all records and communications, disclosing only as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Sec. 25).
  • Prepare for Department investigation and potential civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation; if found in violation, pay the civil penalty within 60 days after the Department's order (Sec. 30).
